about_jev.instructions: Is the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) about TypeSafe's AI model Jev (or TypeSafe AI)?

category.instructions: What is the main kind of the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present)?

criteria.build_demo: The author shows something they built or ran with Jev: an app, tool, bot, experiment or benchmark on their own data
criteria.integration: A company or platform announces Jev is available in or powering its product (gateway, SDK, framework, API integration)
criteria.explainer: Explains what Jev is or how to use it: tutorial, thread, article, guide, ELI5
criteria.news: Reports the launch or news about TypeSafe/Jev (funding, founder, release) without building anything
criteria.opinion: Gives a personal reaction or opinion about Jev (excited, impressed, curious) without a demo
criteria.critique: Is skeptical or critical of Jev, its claims or its marketing
criteria.official: An official TypeSafe post (announcement, demo, customer result)
criteria.meme: A joke or meme about Jev
criteria.question: Asks a question about Jev or asks for help or access
criteria.unrelated: Not about TypeSafe's Jev model at all (e.g. a person named Jev, another TypeSafe)

domain.instructions: Which application domain does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) relate to?

criteria.social_content: Social media posts, virality, content creation, news-jacking
criteria.coding_devtools: Code review, developer tools, CLI safety, testing
criteria.agents_browser: Agents, browser/computer use, tool calling, agent routing
criteria.games: Games and game bots (Doom, Minecraft, chess…)
criteria.safety_moderation: Safety, moderation, guardrails, spam, content filtering
criteria.data_classification: Generic classification, extraction or labeling of documents or data
criteria.ux_personalization: Adaptive UI, personalization, recommendations, voice interfaces
criteria.research_science: Research papers, science, evaluation, benchmarks of the model itself

pattern.instructions: If the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) describes a system built with Jev, how is Jev used in it?

criteria.batch_classifier: Runs Jev over many items in bulk to label, score or filter them (ads, emails, papers, posts)
criteria.realtime_loop: Calls Jev repeatedly in a live loop to decide the next action (game bot, trading bot, browser agent)
criteria.router: Uses Jev as a switch that routes requests to tools, models, handlers or humans
criteria.reviewer_guardrail: Uses Jev to check or approve another model's output or command before acting
criteria.ranking: Uses Jev to rank or rerank candidates (search results, leads, stories)
criteria.features_for_ml: Turns Jev answers into numeric features for a scoring or prediction model

niche.instructions: Which product niche does the use case in the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) belong to?

criteria.ad_intelligence: Analyzing ads or marketing creatives at scale (hooks, offers, CTAs, competitor ads)
criteria.content_virality: Scoring or improving social media posts, predicting virality, content optimization for creators
criteria.newsjacking_pr: Monitoring news or trends and matching them to brands, PR, press opportunities
criteria.lead_scoring: Scoring sales leads, matching prospects to messages, outreach personalization, buying signals
criteria.email_triage: Classifying, prioritizing or routing emails, inbox triage
criteria.support_routing: Routing or classifying customer support tickets, chat intents, helpdesk automation
criteria.code_review: Reviewing pull requests or code diffs, detecting risky changes, code quality checks
criteria.agent_safety: Guarding AI agents: approving shell commands, permissions, tool-call safety, guardrails
criteria.context_compaction: Compacting or pruning an AI agent's context, memory selection, deciding what to keep in context
criteria.browser_automation: Browser agents or computer use: choosing clicks, typing and navigation on web pages or desktop apps
criteria.qa_testing: Automated QA testing of apps, adversarial testing, test agents
criteria.tool_routing: Routing requests between tools, models or skills; choosing which LLM or handler to use
criteria.search_ranking: Search, reranking results, RAG passage selection, launchers ranking by intent
criteria.data_labeling: Classifying rows of data, spreadsheets, databases, CSV labeling, research paper or document sorting
criteria.moderation: Content moderation, spam, rage bait, scam detection, feed filtering
criteria.trading_signals: Trading decisions, market signals, buy/sell bots, finance
criteria.game_bots: Game-playing bots and game AI (Mario, chess, Minecraft, Doom, NPCs)
criteria.voice_control: Voice commands mapped to actions, voice interfaces
criteria.adaptive_ui: Adaptive or personalized interfaces, recommendations, predictive UX
criteria.robotics_iot: Drones, robots, IoT, physical devices controlled by decisions
criteria.dev_integration: SDKs, libraries, wrappers or plugins that make Jev easier to use for developers (DuckDB, RubyLLM, MCP, languages)
criteria.education_content: Teaching Jev: courses, tutorials, explainers, newsletters about building with Jev

sentiment.instructions: What attitude toward Jev does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) express?
criteria: Hostile: dismissive or calls it hype or a scam

depth.instructions: How much technical detail does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) give about how something works or was built?

passive_potential.instructions: How well could the use case in the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) become a self-serve product that earns recurring revenue with little ongoing work from its owner?
criteria: No product here: a toy, a one-off experiment, or just commentary
Hard to sell: niche curiosity, or needs constant manual work or custom service
Plausible product, but needs sales effort or heavy support
Clear self-serve product with an obvious buyer and recurring use
Strong passive product: buyers already pay for this problem, usage recurs automatically, little upkeep

demand_signal.instructions: Does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) (or the reaction it describes) show that people want this: asking for access, the code, a tool, or saying they need it?

commercial.instructions: Is the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) tied to a commercial product, paid service or startup already selling this use case?

working_demo.instructions: Does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) show a working demo, screenshot or video of Jev in action?

open_source.instructions: Does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) share open source code, a repo, or a free tool people can try?

numbers.instructions: Does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) give concrete numbers about Jev's cost, speed, accuracy or scale?

vs_llm.instructions: Does the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) compare Jev against LLMs such as GPT, Claude, Gemini or Fable?

self_promo.instructions: Is the X post in `post` (with its `quoted_post`, `article` and `video_transcript` when present) also promoting the author's own product, service or course?
